title: Spanish train crash leaves 68 dead, PM Sanchez declares 3 days of mourning
summary: Two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers collided south of Madrid. Spain's transport minister said one of the trains was told to continue its journey despite a "red signal" being in…

image.caption: At least two train carriages derailed and tumbled down an embankmentImage: Manu Fernandez/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: EU flags have been lowered to half-mast in solidarity with Spain
European Union flags have been lowered to half-mast outside the European Commission headquarters in Brussels as a marker of European solidarity.
The Commission said the flags were lowered after Spain declared three days of official mourning.
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced the decision earlier this morning when he visited the crash site near Urda.
Wednesday's crash, which killed at least 68 people according to the latest updates, is the deadliest train disaster in the EU since 2013.
